ArchivedModel.description: GET /api/inbox/threads/archived: Settings' Archived block, newest archived first, a page at a time.

projects.description: Every project with archived threads, and how many, for the block's project filter.

total.description: Archived threads in the filtered scope, beyond this page too.

machines.description: `machines=1`: each linked machine asked, `away` when its rows are the ones it last gave.

DoorError.description: Every refusal: `{ error, code, ...details }`. Act on `code`, never the words (packages/server/inbox-devices.ts `refuse`).

field.description: The body field at fault, on `422 validation_error`.

tries_left.description: `401 pairing_code_wrong`: tries left before the offer closes.

DoorHelloFrame.description: The stream's first frame, `event: hello` (packages/server/inbox.ts, the events handler).

DoorPairAnswer.description: `201` to `POST pair` (inbox-devices.ts: `json({ device, token, secret, computer, addresses, relay }, 201)`).

secret.description: The pairing secret, also when paired by the digits.

relay.description: Null when the relay could not be reached at pairing.

DoorPairRequest.description: `POST pair`: by the QR's secret, or by the six digits typed (inbox-devices.ts, the pair handler).

unsent_only.description: Refuse a question a reply already sent (`409 question_already_sent`).

DoorQuestionPick.description: One question in a pick or a reply.

message_id.description: Another message of the same thread and session (a reply only).

answer.description: Null takes the pick back (a pick only).

DoorRecordFrame.description: `event: record`, with `id: <seq>` (packages/server/inbox.ts `eventPayload`). Kinds are added over time: skip one you do not know.

first.description: `message`: true on the message's first line.

skip.description: Only questions the person chose to skip.

clear_draft.description: The reply draft's `updated_at`, only for words prefilled from that draft.

seen_through_seq.description: The `cursor` of the thread read the person saw (`409 thread_moved_on` when an agent wrote after it).

through_seq.description: The seq of the newest message the phone showed; absent: every agent message so far.

InboxAck.description: The person's 👍 on an agent message (`InboxMessage.ack`). The last line wins, as for every record: settling and the agent's read are new snapshot lines of the same message.

reaction.description: The emoji the person reacted with from the 👍's tray (approval "inbox-reaction-tray"): one of their saved emoji (with its name, when it has one) or any emoji picked once. Absent or null: 👍 Looks good. It can change only inside the Undo window; the agent gets the one the person ended on (the note's `ack_reaction` and `inboxAckLine`), and read_thread shows it (`ack.reaction`).

read_seq.description: The Mark read this ack stands on (the root's `person_read_seq`): Move back on that read withdraws the ack.

made_read.description: This ack made that Mark read (the thread was not read before), so its Undo undoes the read too.

settled_seq.description: Set once the Undo window passed with the ack standing (the seq of that line, and when): agents see it from then on (read_thread). Null before.

note_id.description: The note that carries this 👍 to the agent (`InboxMessage.ack_of`), written when it settled. The note is delivered only while the ack still names it, so a 👍 taken back before its delivery never arrives. Absent on acks settled before the amendment (they were never sent).

not_sent.description: Set when the Undo window ended but the 👍 could no longer go: the person wrote back after the message (`replied`) or the agent wrote again (`wrote_again`) inside the window. No note is written and no agent sees it; the window says it was not sent. Absent on every other ack.

seen_at.description: When an agent read it (read_thread, or the wake delivered its note). Null until then.

delivered_at.description: The window's thread only (`GET /api/inbox/threads/:id`): when the 👍 reached the agent (its note delivered as a turn, or an agent read it), else null. Never stored.

note_at.description: The window's thread only: its note's `created_at`, `deliver_now_at` and `deliver_now_by` (a 👍 that waited on a busy session goes into the running turn by itself after `INBOX_AUTO_SEND_AFTER_MS`). Never stored.

wait_started_at.description: The note's `wait_started_at` and its delivery's `into_turn` (the window's thread only).

InboxActionFacts.description: What an action item's block says besides what to do and why (`InboxQuestionRecord.action`).

where.description: `Where:` in words (a place, or the link's name), or null.

where_url.description: `Where:`'s link, http(s) only, or null: the card's "Open" button.

run.description: `Run:`, a command for the person to copy, or null.

watching.description: `Watching:`, what the agent watches to notice it done by itself, or null.

InboxActionResult.description: What came of an action item (`InboxQuestionRecord.action_result`).

note.description: The person's note with Done, or the reason with Can't do it; null for none.

message_id.description: With `by: "agent"`: the agent's message whose `done` named it.

staged.description: The person's Done or Can't do it waits in their reply draft and goes with their next Send, never on a timer (approval "inbox-action-items-in-reply"). Absent: marked through the timed path (decision mode, the phone door, an older window), sent once the Undo window passes.

person.description: With `by: "agent"`: the person's staged mark the agent's `done` settled (approval "inbox-action-items-in-reply", Q3). When it carries a note, the note still goes with the person's next Send (`inboxActionInDraft`).

InboxAddressee.description: The agent session a person's New message is addressed to (`InboxMessage.to`).

InboxAgent.description: One agent of a machine, as the list model names it for the sidebar's Agents section (`GET /api/inbox/threads`' `agents`; packages/server/inbox-agents-list.ts). An agent is a live session, a session that owns a thread waiting on the person (ended or not), a session that ended today, or a session the Inbox launched (a stopped one is idle).

id.description: Stable while the agent lasts: the launch id for a session the Inbox launched, else the session id.

session.description: The session it runs as now (a launch's placeholder `launch:<id>` until it started).

continues.description: The session ids its conversation had before (a poll's `continues`, nearest first; additive, absent when none): the host gave the conversation a new session id. One of them that still polls is listed as its own agent too.

launch.description: Set when the Inbox launched it: the launch's id and its thread; whether the host started it (`started`), its run line's state (`run`, null: no line) and the name of the scratch folder its Delete removes (`scratch`, null in a project), absent from an older Inbox.

label.description: Its title as its connection last said it (the To picker's name). Absent when none.

title.description: The title its host generated for the session (Claude Code's own session title; INBOX_TITLE_POLL_FIELD), the last one its connection read. Its name when it has no `label`. Absent when none. Additive.

first_thread.description: The thread it got first (the first message it wrote, or a person's to it; a launch's own thread), with that thread's name: its name when it has neither `label` nor `title`. The same thread however many it writes in later. Absent when none is known. Additive.

project.description: The project it works in (`id` null for a folder the Inbox has no project for); null when it never said where.

state.description: `waiting`: it owns `waiting` threads in Stopped on you, Holding up work or Waiting on you (whatever else it does); else `working` (a turn runs, or a launch is starting), `idle` (live, or a launch that is stopped), `ended`.

waiting.description: How many of its threads wait on the person (0 when none).

live.description: Its session is live now (polls, or a launch that a reply starts again); false for an ended one.

started_at.description: When it started; null when this Inbox never heard it start (it only owns a waiting thread).

last_seen_at.description: When this Inbox last heard from it (a poll, a state change, an Inbox tool call, its latest message); null when never.

place.description: Where it lives (`InboxAgentPlace`): a Rex pane Rex confirmed for this read. Absent when none. Additive.

rex_status.description: What that confirmed Rex pane says the agent is doing (OSC 7501's root record, state and kind only), when it says more than the Inbox knows: `blocked` (`state` then `waiting`), `done` or `error` (`state` idle). This computer's own window only. Additive.

rex_mark.description: The status mark on its icon (the owner's "jelly" marks): only for a session the Inbox started in Rex while "Start new agents in" is Rex, as its pane's status record said at a read of the last few seconds (none when stale or missing: today's icon). This computer's own window only. Additive.

InboxAgentFaceEntry.description: One agent's face, and the name the person gave it.

face.description: `agent` (its own mark) only beside a `name` or a `tile`: an entry is kept for a face, a tile, a name, or a mix.

tile.description: A tile choice (`InboxAgentTile`), only beside `face: "agent"`. Absent: none. An older Plannotator passes over it.

sessions.description: Every session id this agent was or is (never its key itself), oldest first.

name.description: The name the person gave it (Rename… on its sidebar row): the window's name for it everywhere, over its own title. Display only: never sent to an agent. Absent: none given. An older Plannotator drops an entry that has a name and no face when it reads the file, and keeps the face of one with both.

InboxAgentPlace.description: Where an agent lives, as this computer's Rex last confirmed it (packages/server/inbox-rex.ts): one quiet line, "Rex · <session> / <tab>" in Rex's own names as of that read. `show`: Show in Rex is offered (the window asking is on this computer, and Rex's app here confirmed a jump in this run and has not failed one since). Additive: absent from an older Inbox, and for an agent whose place Rex does not confirm.

InboxAgentsGroup.description: One machine's agents on the list model (`agents`, one group per machine), in a fixed order: the newest first seen first, an agent keeping its place whatever it does. At most `INBOX_AGENTS_LISTED_MAX`; past that, the ones waiting on the person stay listed.

machine.description: The machine (its `ibx_` id), on the merged view (`machines=1`) only.

total.description: Every agent of the machine, those past the cap included.

faces.description: A linked machine's faces and given names for its agents, as kept there (`inbox/agent-faces.json`; approval "inbox-linked-marks"): in that machine's group on the merged view, and in its own group when a linked machine reads its list. Absent from an older Inbox. `faces_rev` is that file's `rev`.

face_tiles.description: The machine keeps a tile choice (`InboxAgentFaceEntry.tile`; approval "inbox-generated-agent-icons"). Absent from an Inbox from before tiles: the window then draws and offers that machine's agents what it can keep (no tile).

path.description: The file's absolute realpath at send time: the only path ever read.

named_path.description: The path as the agent named it (absolute) when it differs from `path` (a symlink).

sent_sha256.description: The sha256 of the bytes sent: the blob `inbox/blobs/<sent_sha256>`.

size.description: Size in bytes of the sent version.

sent_at.description: When it was sent (the message's time).

sent_mtime.description: The file's mtime when it was sent.

media_type.description: The sniffed content type of the sent bytes (images: `image/png`, ...; PDF: `application/pdf`; video: `video/mp4`, `video/quicktime`, `video/webm`; audio: `audio/mpeg`, `audio/mp4`, `audio/wav`, `audio/ogg`, `audio/flac`, `audio/aac`, `audio/webm`). Added with the image and pdf kinds.

width.description: An image's size in pixels, from its header, when it parses; a video's first video track (MP4/MOV only).

duration_ms.description: A video's length in milliseconds, from `moov/mvhd` (MP4/MOV only, when it parses); a recording's from its header (M4A, WAV, FLAC, MP3, Ogg, when it parses). Additive.

InboxAttachmentKind.description: How the window draws a file: Plannotator's viewer for its type. `code` (a source file, a script, or any other UTF-8 text) is drawn as a code view with line comments; `image` inline in the message and in an image viewer; `video` in a player, with comments at moments; `audio` in a player too, with comments at moments the same way (contract 4: `blockId: "video"`, `inboxVideo.time`); `pdf` and `file` are offered as downloads.

session.description: The asking session: the stdio shim's own `ses_` id, or a host's session id.

name.description: A display name the agent gave itself.

InboxDelivery.description: How a person's reply or New message reached an agent session (`InboxMessage.delivery`).

read_by.description: Settled by a read of another agent (its host), not by the session named here (`InboxMessage.agent_checked_by`).

session.description: The session it was delivered to (the asking message's `author.session`, or the message's `to.session`).

into_turn.description: Written for an item the Inbox marked to go in by itself (approval "inbox-busy-agent-reply"): true when it went into a running turn, false when its session went idle after the mark (the session's own Ask question held the turn, so it went in when the turn ended). Absent otherwise.

InboxDeliveryReason.description: Which case of the rule decided the state, so a client words it exactly as the thread does: `delivered`, `undelivered` (the addressed session stopped before it took it), `stuck` (not delivered: its session's connection took it and stopped mid-delivery, so that session never gets it), `ended` (saved: the session that asked has ended), `reads` (saved: an agent that reads the thread), `sending_now` (Send now pressed), `working` (queued: its session is in a turn), `idle` (sending: the session is idle, the turn goes now), `away` (queued: its session does not poll now), `next_turn` (queued: the Inbox does not know the session's state), `ack_pending` (a 👍 inside its Undo window), `stopped` (queued: Claude Code refused it after the person stopped that session, and holds it until they type there; #2780, approval "inbox-stopped-reply").

InboxDeliveryState.description: delivered ✓✓, not delivered (a warning), saved ✓ (an agent reads it later), queued (a clock), sending (dots).

InboxDevicePublic.description: A device as the routes answer it: everything but the token's hash.

name.description: As the phone sent it, checked like a thread name.

last_seen_at.description: Kept in memory on every request; a line is written when its UTC day changes.

carriage.description: The relay carries this phone's items and pushes (section 4); true at pairing.

refusal_owed_until.description: A linked machine unlinked here while it could not be told (docs/agent-guides/inbox-machines.md): until this time, or until its revoked token has been refused once, the tailnet door stays published so its next contact hears `device_revoked`. Absent otherwise.

project.description: The project it was written in (the chosen session's, or the one open in the list).

thread_name.description: The thread's name the person typed in compose (the chip), as typed. Absent while the chip follows the message (compose's suggestion, worked out again from the body when the draft opens).

card.description: The Board card it was started for (the opened card's Create thread): the Send that sends the draft links the new thread to this card. Absent for any other draft.

pulls.description: The pull requests it was started for (Pull requests' Launch an agent): the Send hands them to the new thread. `projects`: the projects of their repository (To offers only those); `ask_line`: the hand-off's guided-review line as it was offered, so a Send whose words no longer hold it is kept as a custom curation.

board_request.description: Compose's Board chip was on (approval "inbox-compose-board-chip"): the Send asks the agent to track the work on the Board.

start.description: Where a new session would start, when the person picked a folder that is no project yet (approval "launch-create-clone", D8/D9): the agent, the machine (null: this computer), the folder as `~/…`, its name, and `create` when the Send makes it. Reopened, the pick comes back, checked again (a folder there by now is no longer made).

InboxDraftFile.description: A draft's file: an upload not sent yet, and, for a long paste, where it goes back.

duration_ms.description: The film or recording's length, when its metadata can be read.

shown_sha256.description: The listing's stat name for a big changed file this was added from, so the button knows its tile after a reload.

InboxDraftPasted.description: A long paste that became a file (approval "inbox-paste-attachment"): where Put back returns its text in the draft's words. `at` is an offset into the words as saved, `lead` what goes before it (the thread-name chip's space), `preview` the tile's name line (the paste's first words). The text itself is the upload's bytes.

clone.description: Clone from a git URL: the repo the Send clones into `folder` (D8, D9).

InboxDraftTo.description: The session a draft was written for, with enough to name it after it has ended.

InboxGuideRef.description: What a message keeps about the guided review it carries: the blob holding the snapshot (Plannotator's portable format, `@plannotator/core/guide-format`, exactly as validated) and the facts the card and the row draw.

sha256.description: sha256 (hex) of the snapshot JSON, the blob's name under `inbox/blobs/`.

input_sha256.description: sha256 (hex) of what the agent sent (the guide and the patch, or the snapshot, as given). A retry with the same idempotency_key compares this: the built snapshot carries the time it was built, so its own hash differs.

bytes.description: The snapshot JSON's size in bytes.

review.description: The agent asked for a verdict (submit_guide `review: true`, only while the person has Settings → Capabilities → Code review on): the window draws a review card with Start review, and the person's Approve or Send feedback comes back as their reply. Absent on every other guide.

chapters.description: A review's chapter titles, in order (the card lists them). Only with `review`.

walkthrough.description: A walkthrough: the code as it is, with nothing changed (submit_guide `walkthrough`, or any guide in a thread the New review box started as one). Always with `review`; it takes no verdict, and its patch is context lines only.

source.description: A review's source (Reviews, approval "inbox-reviews-page"): the snapshot's `source` (kind, repo, branch, head, PR) and `review` (base, git ref), each one line. Only with `review`; absent on reviews sent before it (the Reviews index reads those from the snapshot once).

InboxHandoff.description: A hand-off a person's reply carries (`InboxMessage.handoff`).

from.description: The session that owned the thread before; null when there was none.

label.description: The readable label the person picked for the new owner ("Claude Code (herdr)").

settled_at.description: The Undo window passed: the new owner and the former one are handed it.

undone_at.description: Taken back inside the Undo window (the reply went as an Ask instead), or moved back to the former owner later.

version.description: The running binary's version, or `dev` for a source run.

update.description: The sidebar's update button (packages/server/inbox-updates.ts), or null. `available` and `version` keep the older `{ available, version }` shape.

notify_reach.description: Whether a notification can reach the person now (additive; absent from an older Inbox).

event_streams.description: Event streams open now, the windows' and the phone door's (additive). The Inbox tabs of one browser origin share one stream (packages/inbox/sharedEvents.ts).

peek.description: This Inbox honours the peek mark on a read_thread list (`INBOX_PEEK_META_KEY`): no project made for a folder it does not know, the rows not counted as read (additive). A connection reads the session's threads only from an Inbox that says so; an older one would make a project for every folder that compacts or resumes.

inbox_id.description: This Inbox's stable id, which linked machines key on (additive; packages/server/inbox-links.ts).

follows.description: The earlier runs of this Inbox's data folder, newest first (additive; packages/shared/inbox/registry.ts `inboxSessionLineage`).

machine_links.description: The machine-link protocol this Inbox speaks (additive; absent: it cannot link).

machine_update.description: Additive: this Inbox's door takes `update`, so a linked machine can update it.

self_update.description: Additive: the install script owns this copy, so it can update itself.

update_no_change.description: Additive: a linked machine's Update ended with no error and no new binary: the version it was for.

launch_from_machines.description: Remote launch: 1 while a linked machine may start agents here, 0 while launch is off. Absent from an older Inbox.

message_deletions.description: The store takes a Delete on an agent message's words (`type` "DELETION", approval "inbox-toolbar-delete"; 1). Absent from an older Inbox, whose store refuses one (422): a linked machine's window says it needs an update.

window_controls.description: The page honours `--pn-window-controls-width` and `-height` on `:root`, for a desktop host that draws the window's buttons over it, and from 2 names the line they go on in `--pn-window-controls-center-y` (additive; absent from an older Inbox).

InboxInlineImage.description: An image a message's body shows (`![alt](design/b.png)` or ``), captured as a file of the thread (approval "inbox-image-viewer", 2026-10-15): the store reads it under the message-image route's rules (referenced in the body, an image by extension and by its bytes, inside the message's project or the linked worktree it was sent from, at most 10 MB and 50 megapixels), copies its bytes into a blob and keeps this record on the message (`InboxMessage.inline_images`). It is an attachment record (an `att_` id, the realpath, the sent blob) plus `ref`, so every attachment route, comment and export path reaches it by id; the window steps through it with the attachments. Additive: a reader that does not know the field draws nothing extra.

ref.description: The src exactly as the body wrote it (`design/checkout-b.png`), what the body's image renders from.

captured.description: `"on_open"`: the message was sent before images were captured, and the store took this copy the first time the thread was read ("Changed since you first opened it"). Absent: captured when the message was sent.

captured_at.description: When it was captured on open; absent when captured at send.

path.description: The file's absolute realpath at send time: the only path ever read.

named_path.description: The path as the agent named it (absolute) when it differs from `path` (a symlink).

sent_sha256.description: The sha256 of the bytes sent: the blob `inbox/blobs/<sent_sha256>`.

size.description: Size in bytes of the sent version.

sent_at.description: When it was sent (the message's time).

sent_mtime.description: The file's mtime when it was sent.

media_type.description: The sniffed content type of the sent bytes (images: `image/png`, ...; PDF: `application/pdf`; video: `video/mp4`, `video/quicktime`, `video/webm`; audio: `audio/mpeg`, `audio/mp4`, `audio/wav`, `audio/ogg`, `audio/flac`, `audio/aac`, `audio/webm`). Added with the image and pdf kinds.

width.description: An image's size in pixels, from its header, when it parses; a video's first video track (MP4/MOV only).

duration_ms.description: A video's length in milliseconds, from `moov/mvhd` (MP4/MOV only, when it parses); a recording's from its header (M4A, WAV, FLAC, MP3, Ogg, when it parses). Additive.

InboxLaunchAgent.description: Launch (start an agent from compose): the agents the Inbox can start a session of, one per line: Claude Code (`claude --bg`), Pi (`pi --mode rpc`, owned by the Inbox), Codex (`codex app-server`, owned by the Inbox).

InboxLaunchClone.description: A launch's clone (`InboxLaunchRecord.clone`): the repo, as the words name it and as git is given it, and where the clone stands. Its percent is never stored (the run line reads it from the running clone).

url.description: What git is given (`parseInboxGitUrl`'s rebuilt URL): https or ssh, never a credential.

error.description: `failed`: why, in the four the run line says (E4 sign-in, E5 no such repo, E6 network, else failed).

error_text.description: `failed` with `error: "failed"`: git's last words, for the line.

renamed_from.description: E11: the folder the Send named was taken by then: that name, as the person knows it (`~/…`).

brings.description: After the clone, what the repo brings that needs the person's trust first (E10): "hooks", "MCP servers", "settings".

ended_at.description: `failed` or `cancelled`: when it ended. Only a reply written after it clones again (E7), never one the clone already had.

InboxLaunchError.description: Why a launch did not start (`InboxLaunchRecord.error`): `untrusted` folder, the CLI `missing`, or anything else.

text.description: One sentence for the run line (screen 14).

InboxLaunchFrom.description: The linked machine a launch was started from: its Inbox id (`ibx_…`) and its name as this Inbox knows it.

InboxLaunchRecord.description: On the root of a thread the person started by launching an agent: written with the root, then once more when the host answers (`session_ref`, or `error`). Live state is never stored; the server computes `InboxRun` on read. Per-launch files live in `<dataDir>/inbox/launch/<id>/`.

session_ref.description: The host's own short id (`claude attach <ref>`); null until it started.

session.description: The session it started as, which the root's `to` stops naming once the root moves. Absent until it started, and on an older launch (`inboxLaunchedSession`).

folder.description: The folder it runs in: the project root, or the scratch folder the Inbox made (its real path).

scratch.description: A new scratch folder (`<scratch root>/<slug>`): Delete purges and removes it. Never a project folder.

scratch_inode.description: A scratch folder's identity when the Inbox made it (`<dev>:<ino>`): Delete purges and removes the folder only while the same folder is still there, never one made later at that path.

made_folder.description: Create a folder (approval "launch-create-clone", A13): the Send made this folder. It stays when the agent doesn't start (the failed line says so, E8); a thread that was never written removes it again while it is empty.

made_inode.description: With `made_folder`: the folder's identity when it was made (`<dev>:<ino>`), so only that folder is ever removed.

clone.description: Clone from a git URL (approval "launch-create-clone"): the repo cloned into `folder` before the agent starts.

full_permissions.description: Started with Settings → Agents' full permissions (bypass mode): the thread's header says so.

own_mode.description: Started in the person's own Claude `permissions.defaultMode` (no `--permission-mode`). Neither this nor full: auto mode.

bypass_available.description: The person recorded Claude Code's bypass consent when the launch was made: it starts with `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`, and its card offers Full permissions. Absent (an older launch too): no Full permissions.

model.description: Fixed at Send, so Try again and every restart start the same.

primary_agent.description: OpenCode's own primary agent the session started as (build, plan, …); absent: its default.

deleted_at.description: The ⋯ menu's Delete removed the session and its files; the thread stays, with no run line.

from.description: Started from a linked machine's window (remote launch): which one. Where the click came from, never a credential. Absent: this computer.

rex.description: Settings → Agents' "Start new agents in" said Rex when it was made (fixed at Send): the agent runs in a tab of Rex (superlogical.com/rex) instead of in the background, and Rex owns its process. `line`: where Rex put it ("Rex · <session> / <tab>") once the tab was made; `unavailable`: Rex was not on this computer at the start, so it started in the background as usual; `refused`: Rex answered the ask with an error (it made nothing), so it started in the background as usual. Empty until the start.

InboxLaunchRex.description: `InboxLaunchRecord.rex`. `session` and `block`: the Rex session and the pane Rex made for it (Stop closes that pane).

InboxListGroupId.description: A group the list draws: a section, the Priority group above them all (`INBOX_PRIORITY_GROUP`), or the Snoozed band under Quiet (`INBOX_SNOOZED_BAND`). The server places no row in either: the window draws them from the row. The window's Archived group under them all (approval "inbox-archived-group") reads its own rows, never the list's.

InboxListRow.description: One row of the list: a thread (owner ruling 2026-10-07, "a row is a thread"), with its project as a label and a filter, placed in its section.

machine.description: The machine whose Inbox owns the thread (its stable `ibx_` id), on rows of the merged view only (`GET /api/inbox/threads?machines=1`; linked machines, packages/server/inbox-machines.ts). Absent on this Inbox's own list.

thread_name.description: The thread's name (send_message's `thread`), or null for an unnamed thread.

latest_preview.description: The row's grey line (approval "inbox-row-latest-preview"): the thread's latest message as plain text, cut near `INBOX_ROW_PREVIEW_MAX` characters (core inbox-row-preview.ts): the newest unread agent message while one is unread, else the newest message, the person's own reply as "You: …". Null when there is nothing to show: an unnamed thread whose latest message is its first (its title already says it), or a message with no words. Only on the list model the window and the phone read (an agent's list row never carries it). Absent from an older Inbox: the window then shows the subject under a named thread, as before.

session_ended.description: The session this thread would reach has ended, as the thread's own note and the delivery line know it (only a host that can tell: a waking connection, not heard from past the grace). Never in Quiet. Absent otherwise.

unread.description: Waiting on the person or new to them: drawn bold. Not for a row in New only for the person's own unsent words or comments (`unsent`).

answered_not_sent.description: No question is open, some are picked and not sent: it waits only for Send.

unsent.description: What the person has not sent in this thread yet (approval "inbox-reply-drafts"): words typed in the reply box (`reply_at`, when they were last saved; null when none), picks saved and not sent, and comments (on attached files, the guided review or the messages) waiting for a Send. Null when nothing is unsent. A thread holding any of it never sits in Quiet unless it is archived. Additive: absent from an older Inbox.

waiting_since.description: When the oldest open question was asked, or null when none is open.

pinned_at.description: When the person pinned the thread to the sidebar (approval "inbox-pinned-threads"), or null. Only on the list model the window and the phone read (`GET /api/inbox/threads`), never on anything an agent reads. Additive: absent from an older Inbox.

tags.description: The live tags the thread is in (approval "inbox-thread-tags"), `ini_` ids, oldest tag first; absent when none. Like `pinned_at`, only on the list model the window and the phone read, never on anything an agent reads.

snoozed.description: The thread is snoozed (approval "inbox-snooze"; the rules are core's inbox-snooze.ts), or null. Like `pinned_at`, only on the list model the window and the phone read, never on anything an agent reads. Additive: absent from an older Inbox.

priority.description: The thread is in the list's Priority group (`inboxRowInPriority`), or null. `person`: the person added it (`inbox/priority.json`), `at` when; `ask` is always null: no agent can set one. Like `pinned_at`, only on the list model the window and the phone read, never on anything an agent reads. Every row from an Inbox that keeps priority carries the key; absent from an older Inbox (no menu item, no group). A linked machine's row carries that machine's own (approval "inbox-linked-marks": the add lives on the thread's machine).

snooze_back.description: The thread came back from a snooze at this time and has not been read since: the row's small clock. Only on the list model, like `snoozed`.

steps_waiting.description: A checklist in this thread has a step waiting on the person (approval "inbox-checklist-spinners-2026-11-07", the calm row): the row's still amber pause. Only while the person's Checklist switch is on, and only on the list model the window and the phone read, never on anything an agent reads. Absent otherwise, and from an older Inbox.

pulls.description: The thread's PRs (approval "inbox-pr-binding"): how many, and the one the row's mark shows with its last known state. Only on this Inbox's own rows of the list model the window reads; absent when the thread has none, and from an older Inbox.

hide_pulls.description: The thread's open PRs that are not hidden (keys; the server's inbox-pull-hidden.ts): the row menu's and the picks' "Hide pull request". Only on this Inbox's own rows of the list the window and the phone read; absent when none. A thread whose open PRs are all hidden is left out of that list (it stays in search and in Reviews' Hidden).

unseen.description: Agent messages after the person's last look (a reply of theirs counts as a look; the Inbox's own notes, `isInboxNote`, do not).

wakes.description: It goes to a session whose connection delivers it as a turn by itself (the asking message came through a waking connection, or the person addressed it to a live session): "Queued for <agent>", not "Saved for". Absent from an older Inbox.

read_by.description: Settled by a read of another agent than the one it was for: that agent's host ("Read by Claude Code, 6:25 PM"). Absent otherwise, and on a thread from before this was recorded.

recipients.description: When the reply tags agents (`InboxMessage.tags`): every session it goes to, the owner first, each with its own delivery ("1 of 3 delivered"). `checked_at` is then set once every recipient a connection wakes has it. Absent otherwise and from an older Inbox.

sent.description: The person's reply is the last message, the Inbox's own notes read past: when, and when the agent read it (null until it has).

participants.description: When more than one agent session is in the thread (it wrote there or the person tagged it): all of them, the thread's first agent first, for the overlapping marks. Absent with one session and from an older Inbox.

last_agent_at.description: When the latest agent message arrived (`last_at` also moves on the person's messages and the Inbox's notes). The window's held list counts agent activity by it. Absent from an older Inbox.

guide.description: A message in the thread carries a guided review: the row's "Guided review" mark.

guide_walkthrough.description: The thread's latest guide is a walkthrough: the same mark says Walkthrough.

addressee.description: On a thread the person started (`started_by_person`): the agent session it is addressed to now (the root's `to`, which "Send to another session" may change), so the row draws that agent's mark and "To <agent>". Absent on every other thread and from an older Inbox.

run.description: On a launched thread (the window's list only): the one muted word after the agent's mark ("Starting", "Working"). Absent otherwise and from an older Inbox.

combining.description: The window's own drawing (approval "inbox-multi-select"): the thread is in a Combine still waiting for its new thread, so the row says "Combining…". No server sends it.

read_at.description: When the person marked the thread read (Mark read), while it still holds: no message but a set-aside note since. The row is Quiet. Null otherwise. Absent from an older Inbox.

ack.description: The person's 👍 on the latest agent message, while the Mark read it made still holds: the row says "👍 Looks good" in place of "Read". Null otherwise. Absent from an older Inbox.

agent_after_archive.description: The thread is archived (resolved) and an agent wrote in it after the archive line (a reply_to reply). Those later messages behave as an open thread's (their questions live and answerable, a reply goes to them); the thread stays resolved until the person acts. Derived from the log, never stored. Absent from an older Inbox.

back_from_archive.description: `agent_after_archive`, and something there still waits: an agent message after the archive the person has not looked at, a live question open or picked, or the person's reply after the archive the agent has not read (not once a Mark read made after it stands: Mark read sends a came-back thread back to the archive). The thread is back in the list, placed as an open thread would be; once handled it returns to the archive on its own. Derived. Absent from an older Inbox.

reask_pending.description: The thread's last message (the Inbox's notes read past) is the person's Re-ask note: the row sits in Sent until the agent asks again (owner's rule, approval "inbox-reask"). Absent from an older Inbox.

delivery.description: Where the person's latest sent item in the thread is (approval "inbox-row-delivery", "Ticks"): their reply or message when it is the thread's last message (the Inbox's notes read past), else a 👍 Looks good on the latest agent message once the Inbox sent it through. Computed with the rule the thread's delivery line uses (`inboxDeliveryState`) from the live sessions, so a row and its thread agree. Null when there is none (an agent wrote last, a 👍 not sent). Absent from an older Inbox.

waits.description: What the row's Stopped / Holds up badge holds (approval "inbox-row-badges", hover card A): each open question or action item that stops the agent or holds something up, in thread order, at most `INBOX_ROW_WAITS_MAX`, its words capped (`INBOX_ROW_WAIT_TEXT_MAX`, `INBOX_ROW_WAIT_HOLDS_MAX`). Absent when none does, and from an older Inbox (the card then lists `questions.holds_up`). The window's list only: agents' rows never carry it.

waiting_on_person.description: The last message is an agent's and the thread is open: it waits on the person. The Inbox's own notes (`isInboxNote`) are read past, and it is false while a Mark read stands (nothing waits on the person then).

InboxLiveSiteRef.description: A running local app a thread shows through the Inbox's loopback live proxy (`packages/server/inbox-live.ts`): today, a question choice's prototype (`Prototype: http://localhost:…`). `id` is `liv_` + 16 hex of the URL's normalized identity, the same in every thread.

url.description: The URL as checked: http, a loopback host, path and query kept, no fragment.

opened_by.description: Who named it: an agent (a choice's `Prototype:` line). "person" is reserved for a site the person opens (#2258).

questions.description: Omitted when the message asks no question (the Workspaces rule). The server lists the message's action items (`kind: "action"`) here too, after its questions; a reader that does not know `"action"` must not answer them.

actions.description: Never sent by the server: the Inbox window moves a message's action items here out of `questions` when it reads a thread (packages/inbox/actions.ts), so nothing that picks and sends answers ever meets one.

seq.description: The seq of the message's first line in the event log. Rides only on `GET /api/inbox/threads/:id` (the window's thread), is never stored and is not on the MCP tools: with the root's `person_seen_seq` it tells the window which messages are new since the person's last look, read BEFORE the window records the next look. Absent from an older Inbox.

sent_annotations.description: On a person's reply, on `GET /api/inbox/threads/:id` only: how many of the person's annotations (on attached files or a guided review's diffs) that reply carried. Absent from an older Inbox.

subject.description: Set on a thread's root: the agent's subject, or one derived from the body.

resolved_at.description: On a thread's root: when the thread was resolved, or null while open.

idempotency_key.description: The sender's idempotency key, when one was given.

thread_name.description: The `thread` name the agent sent this message with (send_message's `thread`), else absent or null. On a root it is the thread's name: a named thread is joined by name across sessions; an unnamed root only by reply_to. Added after step 1: older records lack it.

person_seen_seq.description: On a root: the event-log seq up to which the person has looked at the thread (the window's "seen"). Agent messages after it are "New since you looked". Absent until the first look.

person_read_seq.description: On a root: the person's Mark read, the event-log seq when they pressed it and when. While no message but a set-aside note (`set_aside`) came after it, the thread sits in Quiet without being closed; any other message (an agent's, or the person's own reply) ends it without a write. Null after Undo. Absent on records older than Mark read.

person_seen_before_read.description: On a root marked read: `person_seen_seq` before the Mark read (which counts as a look), for its Undo.

set_aside.description: On a person's set-aside note: the questions (`<message id>/<key>`) a Mark read told the asking agent not to wait on. Written once per question, after the Undo window, as a reply to the message that asked. Absent on every other message.

reopened.description: On a person's reopened note: the questions an Undo of Mark read opened again after a set-aside note had named them. Absent on every other message.

ack_of.description: On the note that carries a 👍 Looks good to the agent (amended 2026-10-16): the agent message the person marked. Written once the ack's Undo window passed (its body is `inboxAckLine`), as a reply to that message, and delivered like any reply (the wake) while the ack still names it (`InboxAck.note_id`). The window and read_thread do not list it: the ack on the message says it. Absent on every other message.

ack_reaction.description: With `ack_of`: the tray reaction the ack had when its Undo window closed (approval "inbox-reaction-tray"), so the wake says the emoji the person ended on (`inboxAckLine`); it never changes after that. Absent for 👍 Looks good and on notes written before.

reask.description: On the person's Re-ask note (approval "inbox-reask"): the open questions (`<message id>/<key>`) it asked the agent to ask again, together in one new message, with `Replaces:` lines for those still needed. It is the person's reply (never an Inbox note): delivered like one, and while it is the thread's last message the row sits in Sent. Picks the person had made but not sent go with it as answers. Absent on every other message.

tidy.description: On a Tidy note (the person's Tidy, 2026-10-28): its run, and whether it is the one note of its session that carries the wake (`wake`; the others only show in their threads and are never delivered). An Inbox note: the row never moves for it. Absent on every other message.

agent_checked_seq.description: On a root: the seq up to which the asking agent has read the person's replies (a wake delivered one, or read_thread read the thread), and when. A Sent row moves to Quiet once its reply is checked.

agent_checked_by.description: The host of the agent whose read moved `agent_checked_seq`, when it is known not to be the agent the reply was for (another host's session, new to the thread, settled a reply no connection wakes). Absent otherwise, and on a thread from before this was recorded: those keep "Delivered".

attachments.description: The files an agent attached (send_message's `attachments`), recorded at send time and read only by their ids (see inbox-attachments.ts). Added in step 2: older records lack it.

inline_images.description: On an agent's message: the images its body shows, captured as files of the thread (`InboxInlineImage`), in the order the body shows them. Written when the message lands, or, for a message sent before images were captured, the first time its thread is read (each record then marked `captured: "on_open"`). Present (possibly empty) once capture ran; absent on a message whose body shows no local image, and on older records.

live_sites.description: On an agent's message: the running apps its question choices name as prototypes (`Prototype: http://localhost:…`), each checked and probed when it was sent (packages/server/inbox-live.ts). Absent otherwise.

delivery.description: On a person's reply: it reached the asking agent's session as a turn through an agent connection (the Claude Code mod), and when. Absent until then; a reply the agent read through the MCP has none. "Replied" is not stored: it is the asking session's next message in the thread. Added in step 6: older records lack it.

t3_wait.description: On a person's reply or message for a T3 Code thread: why the T3 wake cannot put it in now (packages/server/inbox-t3-wake.ts). Absent while nothing known holds it, and dropped when it is delivered.

deliver_now_at.description: On a person's reply or message not yet delivered: the person pressed Send now in the Inbox, and when. The session's connection then delivers it at once, into the running turn when one runs, instead of waiting for the session to go idle (the bridge command's `now`). Absent otherwise and on older records.

deliver_now_by.description: Who asked for `deliver_now_at`: the person (Send now) or the Inbox after the item waited `INBOX_AUTO_SEND_AFTER_MS` on a busy session whose connection can take it mid-turn (approval "inbox-busy-agent-reply"). Kept when a failed attempt clears `deliver_now_at`, so the Inbox never tries by itself twice. Absent on older records (a person's Send now).

wait_started_at.description: When it began to wait on its busy session, written with the Inbox's own mark (`deliver_now_by: "auto"`), so "went into its turn by itself after N min" stays true after delivery. Absent otherwise. Additive.

sent_again_to.description: Try again on a launched session's turn that ended in an error (`InboxRun.turn_error`): the session this message goes to once more, though a read already settled it. It counts only while `delivery` is unset. Absent otherwise. Additive.

turn_error.description: The Inbox's note for a launched session's turn that ended in an error ("<Agent>'s turn ended with an error: …", Claude Code, Codex and Pi): the window notifies for it ("<project>: <agent> couldn't answer"). Written only by the Inbox itself, never by an agent's call. Absent otherwise. Additive.

guide.description: A guided review this message carries (submit_guide, PLAN step 5): the snapshot is a content-addressed blob, `inbox/blobs/<sha256>`. Absent on every other message and on records older than step 5.

guide_reviewed.description: On a message carrying a guide: the person's reviewed tick per section, as the window's guide viewer last saved it (the record's 4.2, "kept with the thread"). Absent until the first tick; the snapshot's own ticks apply then.

guide_viewed.description: On a message carrying a review (`guide.review`): the files the person ticked Viewed in the review, as the patch names them. Absent until the first tick.

review_verdict.description: On the person's reply that gave a verdict on a review (Approve or Send feedback in the review's header): which review, the verdict, and how many of their comments rode it. The review card shows it as its outcome. Absent on every other message.

review_comments_of.description: The reviews (message ids) whose diff comments this person's reply carried (code review in the Inbox), whichever message the reply answers. Set by the store at Send; the window reads it to tell a review happened.

quote.description: On a person's reply that quotes a message of the thread (approval "inbox-reply-quote"): the message, and the words selected in it (absent: the whole message). The store wrote the lead the agent reads at the start of the person's words (`inboxReplyQuoteLead`); the window draws this as one quiet line over the reply instead. Absent on every other message and on older records.

to.description: On a person's New message (plan step 8): the live agent session it is addressed to. Such a message answers nothing (`reply_to` null) and is delivered to that session as a turn, like a reply. Also on a person's reply (`reply_to` set) when the session that asked had ended and the person chose another live session to take it: that session alone is handed it. Absent on every other message and on records older than step 8.

base_path.description: On an agent's message: the realpath of the `project_path` it was sent from, when that is a folder inside the project other than its root. Relative image paths in the body start there (#1813); absent, they start at the project root. Added after step 8: older records lack it.

from_project.description: On an agent's message sent into a thread of another project (`reply_to` from another folder): the project its `project_path` is in, by name (approval "inbox-reply-recipient"). The window names the agent by it ("in plannotator", "Claude Code (plannotator)") after its session ends. Absent for a send from the thread's own project (or a project combined with it), and on older records.

wakes.description: On an agent's message: it was sent through a connection that wakes its session with the person's reply (the Claude Code mod, Pi, OpenCode 2; `INBOX_WAKES_META_KEY`). Only such a session can be said to have ended when it stops polling; an MCP-only agent or OpenCode 1 never polls, so the window never calls it ended. Absent otherwise and on older records.

supersedes.description: On an agent's message: the earlier questions it said it supersedes (send_message's `supersedes`, as sent: `<message id>` for every open question of that message, or `<message id>/<key>` for one). The question records carry the result (`InboxQuestionRecord.superseded_by`); this is what the agent asked for, so a retry with another list is refused. Absent when it superseded nothing through the argument (a `Replaces:` line rides the body). Added for replaced questions: older records lack it.

done.description: On an agent's message: the action items it said it saw done (send_message's `done`, as sent: `<message id>` for every open action item of that message, or `<message id>/<key>` for one). The action item records carry the result (`action_result` with `by: "agent"`). Absent otherwise and on older records.

action_report.description: On a person's reply that reports action items (Done, Can't do it): the action items it reports (`<message id>/<key>`), sent once the Undo window passed. Absent on every other message.

subject_question.description: On a thread's root whose subject the agent did not give: the question (`<message id>/<key>`) the subject was derived from, so the thread's subject follows that question's `superseded_by` chain. Null when the subject was the agent's own or came from the body's first line (it never changes). Absent on records older than replaced questions: then a subject equal to the root's first question's prompt counts as derived from it.

started_by_person.description: On a thread's root the person wrote (compose: "send a new message to a connected agent"): the thread was started by the person, addressed to one live agent session (`to`). The agent's answer lands in it by `reply_to`. Absent on every other message.

board_request.description: On the root of a thread the person started with compose's Board chip on (approval "inbox-compose-board-chip", 2026-10-27): the person asked the agent to track the work on the Board. The body stays as typed; what the agent receives for this message (the delivered turn, read_thread) carries `inboxBoardRequestBlock` after it. Absent on every other message.

decision_ask.description: On the root of a thread the person started from Settings -> Decision data's Ask. The body stays as typed; what the agent receives for this message (the delivered turn, read_thread) carries `INBOX_DECISION_ASK_BLOCK` after it. Absent on every other message.

rows_ask.description: On the root of a thread the person started from Settings → Rows' ask box. The body stays as typed; what the agent receives for this message carries `INBOX_ROWS_ASK_BLOCK` (inbox-rows-words.ts) after it. Absent on every other message.

viewing.description: On a person's reply sent from full screen's floating box: the file on screen. Rendered for the agent at read time; the body never holds it.

launch.description: On the root of a thread the person started by launching an agent (To: "New Claude Code session"), or on a person's reply sent to a new session in place of one that ended (the reply box's "New Claude Code session" row). Absent on every other message.

scheduled_run.description: A routine's run divider or skip line (inbox-scheduled-types.ts). A divider also carries its run's `launch`.

scheduled_change.description: An agent's `routine` change, posted as that agent in the thread it called from.

message_id.description: The reply that carried the name.

named_by.description: On the root of a thread the person started: who gave it its name, the thread chip (approval "inbox-agent-names-own-thread"). The person may name it in compose; otherwise the first reply from a session that may name it (`InboxStore.canNameThread`) carrying a valid `thread` names it, once, and the root is written again with the name and this field. Absent while the thread has no name, and on every other message. A name set here is never replaced, except compose's suggestion (`kind: "auto"`), which the first agent that may name the thread replaces.

reply_thread.description: On an agent's reply: the `thread` it carried, as given (trimmed), so a retry with the same idempotency key and another `thread` is told apart. Absent when it carried none, and on every other message.

thread_naming.description: On an agent's reply into a thread the person started that it could name: what the naming came to (`InboxThreadNaming`), so a retry answers the same. Absent everywhere else.

ack.description: On an agent's message: the person's 👍 Looks good (design record "inbox-acknowledge", approved 2026-10-15, amended 2026-10-16). The thread is marked read; once the Undo window passes the Inbox sends it to the agent (a note, `note_id`), delivered like a reply. Null after Undo. Absent on every other message and on older records.

tags.description: On a person's reply: the agent sessions they tagged with `@` (approval "inbox-tag-agents", Lines variant), in the order typed, never the session the reply goes to anyway (its owner, `InboxStore.recipientOf`). ONE message, handed to its owner and to every tagged session; each records its own delivery in its entry, so each gets its own line and Send now. A message with tags is settled for each recipient only by that recipient's own delivery, or for one not woken its own read, never by another agent's read. Absent on every other message and on older records.

handoff.description: On a person's reply that handed the thread to another session (the reply box's "Hand off instead", approval "inbox-tag-handoff", option A2): the reply's `to` is the new owner, and every later reply in the thread goes to it. `from` is the session that owned the thread before (it gets a notice: a tag with `handed_away`). Held for the Undo window: nobody is handed the reply until `settled_at` is set. `undone_at`: the person took the hand-off back inside that window; the reply then went as an Ask (a tag) and no longer moves the thread. Absent on every other message.

took_over.description: A person's reply whose `to` took the place of a session that had ended (the recipient pill, or Send to another session). Until an agent writes again the person's next reply follows its `to`. Set only by the server, which checks the session really ended; a reply aimed elsewhere while the asker is live does not carry it.

InboxNotifyReach.description: Whether a browser notification can reach the person now (packages/server/inbox-windows.ts): notifications come from an open Inbox tab, so with none open, or none the browser lets notify, nothing reaches them. `windows`: Inbox tabs holding an event stream; `allowed`: those whose browser reported `granted`; `allowed_origins`: their addresses.

InboxParticipant.description: Who a thread involves, for the overlapping marks on the row and the thread head: the distinct agent sessions that wrote in it or were tagged in it, the thread's first agent first. `name` is an MCP agent's own name.

InboxProject.description: One row of the window: the repository or folder an agent works in.

key.description: The folder name under `inbox/projects/`: `<name>-<6 hex of the root>`.

root.description: Absolute realpath of the repository root (git toplevel) or folder.

display_name.description: The name the person gave the project (Rename… in the project menu), shown as it is in place of its folder's name. Additive: absent until someone renames, and absent again after Reset name. Id, key, `name` (the slug) and root never change with it.

merged_into.description: The project this one was combined into (approval "project-combine"). Every reader shows this project's threads under the end of that chain; nothing of this project moves, and an older reader ignores the field. A target that is gone, or a loop, counts as not combined, so a project can only reappear.

separated_from.description: The project this one's last undone combine went into: Tidy does not suggest the pair again.

InboxProjectRepo.description: The repository a project's git `origin` names (#1840): its path on the forge (`owner/repo`, or a GitLab `group/sub/project`) and the remote's host, null when the host did not parse. The window links bare `#123` refs with it.

InboxQuestion.description: A question as the window and the agents read it: Workspaces' `Question` exactly (`asked_by_checked_at` omitted, as Workspaces omits it outside its two comment lists), plus the Inbox's `message_id`.

kind.description: `"action"` for an action item; read it with `readInboxQuestionKind` (fail-closed).

set_aside_at.description: When the person's Mark read closed it unanswered (`state: "closed"`, answer a skip), or null. Absent from an older Inbox.

action.description: On an action item (`kind: "action"`): where, run and watching. Absent on a question and from an older Inbox.

action_result.description: On an action item: what came of it, or null while open. Absent on a question and from an older Inbox.

attachment.description: A question inside an attached Markdown file (`InboxQuestionRecord.attachment`). Absent: a question of the body, or an older Inbox.

shows.description: `Shows:` — the one picture (`image`) or file (`link`) the decision is about, its src as written.

reversible.description: `Reversible: no — <why>`: the answer cannot be taken back. Absent means reversible.

prototype.description: `Prototype:` at the block's own indent: one page every option shows (approval "inbox-question-tradeoffs"), as written.

InboxQuestionAttachment.description: Where a question inside an attached Markdown file sits (issue #2828): the file the message attaches, and the question's key as that file's own cards compute it (`findQuestionBlocks` over the sent text). The record's `key` is unique among the message's questions (a body question keeps its key; a file's question takes the next free `-N` when a body question or an earlier file has it), and is the one a pick, a supersede and a reply name. The record's `position` is its place among that file's questions (Q1 is the file's first card), and `parsed.line` its prompt's line in the file.

id.description: The attachment's `att_` id on the same message.

name.description: The file's name, as the message's attachment record names it.

key.description: The question's key inside the file (what its card computes).

InboxQuestionChoice.description: One choice as the wire serves it (Workspaces' `QuestionChoice`).

image.description: A picture choice (`- [ ] Label — ![alt](path)`): the image, its src as the body writes it (the message image route and the captured `inline_images` take that same src). Present only on a picture choice; absent from records written before picture choices.

pros.description: Option lines (approval "inbox-question-tradeoffs"), each indented under a `- [ ]` choice and read at send: `Pros:` and `Cons:` items (split on `;`), and `Prototype:`, the page that shows this option as written (an attached HTML file's path, or an `http://` address of an app running on this computer, checked at send and kept in the message's `live_sites`). Each is absent when the choice names none, and on older records.

InboxQuestionKind.description: A question's kind as the Inbox stores it: Plannotator's question kinds, plus `"action"` for an action item (approval "inbox-next-actions").

InboxQuestionState.description: Derived, never stored. `superseded`: the agent replaced or withdrew the question (`superseded_by`); it wins over `closed`, so a resolved thread's card still says what replaced it. `closed`: the thread is archived, or the person's Mark read closed the question (`set_aside_at`).

open.description: Open questions and action items together: an action item counts like a question for every list rule.

actions.description: How many of `open` are action items (`kind: "action"`): the row reads "1 action item". Absent from an older Inbox.

staged.description: Action items the person marked Done or Can't do it that wait in their reply draft, the agent still stopped on them (approval "inbox-action-items-in-reply", Q2): the row keeps its section by their Stopped / Holds up (`stopped` and `holds_up` count them). Absent: none.

InboxReaction.description: The person's reaction tray (approval "inbox-reaction-tray"): an emoji and the name they gave it (optional). An ack's `reaction`, and each of the saved emoji (config.json `inboxReactions`, through GET and POST /api/inbox/settings `reactions`).

label.description: The person's name for it ("Ship it"); absent when they gave none.

InboxRecordKind.description: `card`: a Board card (approval "inbox-board"); `steps`: one agent session's steps in a thread (approval "inbox-thread-steps"); `initiative`: a Board initiative (approval "board-initiatives"); `thread_pull`: one PR on one thread (approval "inbox-pr-binding"); `scheduled`: a routine (inbox-scheduled-types.ts). A reader that does not know a kind skips its lines.

InboxReplyQuote.description: The quote a person's reply carries (approval "inbox-reply-quote"): a message of the thread and, when the person selected some, its words.

words.description: The words selected in it, as shown on screen. Absent: the message as a whole.

InboxReplyViewing.description: What was on screen when the person sent a reply from full screen's floating box. Context for the agent, not a choice: it never touches the words, and only the agent's read gets it (`inboxViewingLine`), never the thread.

message_id.description: The message that carries the file.

time.description: That message's time, in the person's own time zone.

page.description: A page the attached HTML page links to, when that page is the one on screen.

as_sent.description: They had the version sent open, and the file has changed since.

InboxRestartAgents.description: The live sessions a reload brings up to date (for Claude Code, also after a plugin update: `update_first`), per runtime: the sidebar's "Reload Claude Code N" ("Reload agents N" when more than one runtime has some). Additive beside `restart_claude_code`.

update_first.description: Of the Claude Code ones, those whose plugin on disk is itself behind this Inbox (`update_plugin`): the plugin update comes before `/reload-plugins`. Additive; absent when none.

InboxReviewSource.description: Where a review's changes came from: the guide snapshot's `source` and `review` (base), as the message records them.

kind.description: The snapshot's kind: local changes, a PR, a workspace, a commit.

repo.description: `owner/repo` or a folder name, as the producer knew it.

base.description: The branch or ref the diff runs from ("origin/main").

pr.description: The PR the guide is of, when it says.

InboxReviewVerdict.description: The person's verdict on a review.

InboxReviewVerdictRecord.description: What a person's verdict reply records (on the reply: `review_verdict`).

comments.description: How many of the person's comments on the review rode the reply.

InboxRexMark.description: A Rex pane's status as a mark: OSC 7501's state, and for `blocked` its kind.

InboxRowDelivery.description: The delivery of the person's latest sent item in a thread, on its list row (`InboxListRow.delivery`): a reply, a message the person addressed to a session (a thread they started, a New message, a reply sent to another session), or a 👍 Looks good the Inbox sent through. Computed by the server from the store and the live sessions with `inboxDeliveryState`.

send_now.description: Send now is offered in the thread (the row never offers it).

message_id.description: The person's message (a reply or message), or the agent message the 👍 is on.

read_by.description: Settled by a read of another agent than the one it was for: that agent's host.

host.description: Whom it goes to: the host of the session (null for an agent without one).

name.description: An MCP agent's own name, when the thread names it by that.

another_session.description: It went to another session of the asker's own host ("Claude Code (another session)").

asking.description: `reason: "ended"`: the agent of the session that asked and has ended (`inboxAskingMessage`), which the line names ("Saved for <it>. The session that asked has ended…"). Absent otherwise.

waiting_since.description: `reason: "working"` (approval "inbox-busy-agent-reply"): it waits on a busy session since then (the first time the server saw that session busy while it waited), the row's "Undelivered N min". Absent otherwise and from an older Inbox. Additive.

steerable.description: With `waiting_since`: its connection can put it into the running turn (the badge is blue; grey otherwise).

auto_send_at.description: With `waiting_since`: when it goes into the running turn by itself; null when it will not.

auto_after_min.description: It went (or is going) into the running turn by itself, after this many whole minutes of waiting.

turn_ended.description: Delivered after an automatic mark, but when the turn ended (the session's own Ask question held it).

t3_wait.description: It waits on T3 (`waitsOnT3`): why, as the thread's line words it (`inboxT3WaitLine`). Absent otherwise. Additive.

InboxRowPriority.description: Why a row is in Priority (`InboxListRow.priority`).

InboxRowSnooze.description: A thread's snooze, on its list row: when it comes back, and when it was snoozed.

InboxRowUnsent.description: What a list row says is not sent yet (`InboxListRow.unsent`).

reply_at.description: When the reply box's words were last saved, or null when the thread holds no reply draft.

comments.description: Comments (on attached files, the guided review, the messages) waiting for a Send.

done.description: Action items marked Done waiting in the reply draft ("Draft · 1 done"; approval "inbox-action-items-in-reply"). Absent: none.

cant.description: Action items marked Can't do it waiting in the reply draft ("Draft · 1 can't do"). Absent: none.

InboxRowWait.description: One question behind a row's badge (`InboxListRow.waits`).

position.description: Its place among its message's blocks of its kind: Q1 is 0 (A1 for an action item, `key` starts `a-`).

InboxRun.description: What a launched thread's run line shows (the thread route's `run`).

since.description: Since when: the start (starting), the turn (working), the prompt (waiting_answer, waiting_terminal), the stop.

stopped_by_person.description: `stopped`: the person pressed Stop (the line names the time).

cause.description: `failed`: the cause in words; `stopped`: the host's note, when it has one (else null); `missing`: null.

untrusted.description: `failed` because the folder is not trusted: Open in Terminal runs plain `claude` there.

turn_error.description: `failed` because the session's last turn ended in an error (its note is in the thread): Try again sends the message again.

home_folder.description: With `untrusted`: the folder is the home folder, which is never trusted (the how-to says to start inside it).

trust_covers_home.description: With `untrusted`: trust here would cover home (a repo rooted there) or the folder is `/`; the how-to says to start in a project with its own repo. Wins over `home_folder`, which home in such a repo carries too, for a window that predates this.

trust.description: With `untrusted`, for the machine's owner when the host can do it: Trust folder, and what would run once trusted.

attach_command.description: `claude attach <ref>` from the folder, for Copy; null before the session exists.

made_folder.description: `failed`, in a folder the Send made (Create a folder): that folder as the person knows it (`~/…`); the line says it was made and stays (E8).

clone.description: A launch that clones first (E1-E11): the repo, the percent once git says one (after a few seconds), why it failed, and what it brings.

rex.description: `held`: a reply waits to start it again, as its old process may still run (`may_run`: the Inbox just started and has not heard from it yet) or still does (`still_runs`: a process runs that session, in its tab or wherever it was resumed). `stops`: the Inbox knows its own pane, so Stop closes it (or, run on in a pane the Inbox did not open, ends just its process).

InboxRunState.description: The run line's state (`packages/core/inbox-run-line.ts`). Absent: no line (the agent is resting).

InboxScheduledChange.description: On a change message an agent's `routine` call posts in the thread it called from ("Made the scheduled thread X…", "Changed…"): the editor link. The body names what changed, old and new.

fields.description: The fields that changed, for an update.

turned_off.description: A folder or agent change turned it off until the person turns it on again.

InboxScheduledRun.description: On a message: the run divider ("Run 4"), which carries the prompt to the run's session as its first turn, or a skip line (`skipped`, no `run`), which goes to nobody. Both are written by the Inbox, authored as the person (the prompt is theirs) and drawn as a line, never as "You".

name.description: The routine's name when this was written (the Inbox row's sender).

due_at.description: The due time it ran for; for Run now, the time it was pressed.

by.description: Who started it: the clock, or Run now from the window or an agent.

missed_before.description: Earlier due times folded into this late run (counted up to 1,000).

skipped.description: On a skip line: the due times skipped (counted up to 1,000), and why.

failed.description: A run that didn't start (the agent missing, the folder gone): why, in the launch's own words.

InboxSectionId.description: The list's sections, in the approved order (Workspaces' inbox model).

InboxSentRecipient.description: Who a person's last message went to, for the Sent row (`InboxListRow.sent.recipients`): the owner first, then the tagged sessions in the order typed.

delivered_at.description: It reached the session; null while it waits.

InboxSupersededBy.description: What superseded a question (`InboxQuestionRecord.superseded_by`): the agent's later message, and the question in it that replaces this one, or null when that message asks nothing in its place ("No longer applies").

InboxTag.description: One agent session a person's reply tags (`InboxMessage.tags`). The last line of the message wins, as for every record: a delivery, a Send now and a read are new snapshots of the whole message.

host.description: The connection's host (`claude-code`, `pi`); null for an MCP agent that never named one.

name.description: The name an MCP agent gave itself, for the person's view only; null otherwise.

label.description: The readable label the person picked, as it reads in their text after `@` ("Pi", "Claude Code (another session)"): the sent message paints that token and names the session's line with it. Absent from an older window.

wakes.description: Its connection wakes it (the Claude Code mod, Pi, OpenCode 2, with the tag capability): the reply arrives as a turn. False: an agent that reads the Inbox only (MCP, OpenCode 1); it sees the tag the next time it reads the thread.

delivery.description: It reached the session (its connection delivered it).

deliver_now_at.description: The person pressed Send now for this session (or the Inbox did, after the wait: `deliver_now_by`).

wait_started_at.description: When it began to wait on that session (see `InboxMessage.wait_started_at`).

read_at.description: A session that is not woken read the thread with read_thread after the tag (its own read only).

joined.description: "Add instead" (approval "inbox-tag-handoff", A2): the person added this session to the thread. It works alongside the owner, and every later reply of the person's in the thread goes to it too (the store tags it again). Absent: an Ask, today's tag (this one message only).

handed_away.description: The former owner's notice on a hand-off reply (`InboxMessage.handoff`): this session is told the thread moved and to stop work on it. Absent on every other tag.

InboxTagColours.description: The switch and the person's own colours, as the list model carries them (`tag_colours`).

show_at.description: When the switch was last set (null: never; it is on).

recent.description: The person's own colours, newest first, at most INBOX_TAG_RECENT_MAX.

InboxTagLook.description: A tag's colour and who set it: `auto` when it was given at creation, `person` once the person picked one or turned Highlight rows off. `colour` is what its rows show; `null` is off (an earlier Inbox's None). Off with a colour kept (the owner: Highlight rows "instantly" on and off, the colour chosen apart): `kept_colour`, so turning it on brings that colour back. An older Inbox ignores the field and reads off as None.

key.description: The folder name under `inbox/projects/`: `<name>-<6 hex of the root>`.

root.description: Absolute realpath of the repository root (git toplevel) or folder.

display_name.description: The name the person gave the project (Rename… in the project menu), shown as it is in place of its folder's name. Additive: absent until someone renames, and absent again after Reset name. Id, key, `name` (the slug) and root never change with it.

merged_into.description: The project this one was combined into (approval "project-combine"). Every reader shows this project's threads under the end of that chain; nothing of this project moves, and an older reader ignores the field. A target that is gone, or a loop, counts as not combined, so a project can only reappear.

separated_from.description: The project this one's last undone combine went into: Tidy does not suggest the pair again.

project.description: `repo` rides only on `GET /api/inbox/threads/:id` and is never stored: the project's `origin`, or null for a folder without one or until the Inbox has resolved it. Absent from an older Inbox. `repo_known` (additive, same read): the Inbox has resolved it, so a null `repo` means the folder has no `origin`, not "not known yet". Absent until then, and from an older Inbox (the window then reads the thread again on each of its records, as before).

thread_name.description: The thread's name, or null for an unnamed thread.

archive_seq.description: The window's read only (`GET /api/inbox/threads/:id`): the seq of the archive line of a resolved thread, null for an open one. A message whose `seq` is after it arrived after the archive and behaves as an open thread's. Absent from an older Inbox and from the MCP tools.

pull_theirs.description: The window's read only: every pull request the person handed to this thread is a teammate's (Pull requests' Hand to an agent; the Inbox's own pull list said so when the owner was kept). Its reviews take no verdict: the owner's direction, "a teammate's PR shows its diff with no verdict". Absent otherwise.

review_started.description: A New review on local changes started this thread: its first message is the box's words, not the person's own.

pull_keys.description: The window's read only, with Code review on: the pull requests the person handed to this thread (their list keys). Its review can be posted to one of them on GitHub/GitLab (`POST /api/inbox/pulls/review`). Absent otherwise.

InboxThreadPullState.description: A coupled PR's state as last read: `unknown` until the reader's first answer (or with no gh or glab).

InboxThreadPullsSummary.description: A list row's PRs, from the stored state: the row paints them without a read of its own.

InboxTidyMark.description: On a Tidy note (`InboxMessage.tidy`): its run, and whether it carries the session's wake.

id.description: The run (`tdy_` + ULID): one press of Tidy, across sessions.

wake.description: The one note of the session that is delivered to it (the wake); the others only show in their threads.

InboxUpdate.description: The Inbox's update control: what the button says and does.

state.description: `available`: a newer release exists, nothing installed yet. `updating`: the install script runs. `ready`: a different binary is on disk (restart to update). `failed`: an install the person started exited non-zero.

action.description: `script`: Update now runs the install script. `copy`: the binary is not the script's; the dialog shows the command.

InboxUpload.description: A file the person uploaded from the window for a thread they start, not sent yet (`POST /api/inbox/uploads`). At send it becomes an `InboxAttachment`; a draft names it by `upload_id`.

duration_ms.description: The film or recording's length, when its metadata can be read.

shown_sha256.description: The listing's stat name for a big changed file this was added from, so the button knows its tile after a reload.

self.description: The merged view (`machines=1`): this Inbox's id and every machine, linked ones with their state. Absent from an Inbox that cannot link; with no machine linked, `machines` holds this Inbox alone.

updated.description: This Inbox started on a newer version than the one before it: "What's new in X" for this run. Absent from an older Inbox.

restart_claude_code.description: Claude Code sessions a /reload-plugins would bring up to date: the sidebar's "Reload Claude Code N". Absent from an older Inbox.

restart_agents.description: Every runtime's sessions a reload brings up to date: the sidebar's "Reload agents N". Absent from an older Inbox.

update_check_failing.description: Checking for updates has failed for hours: the sidebar's quiet "Can't check for updates". Absent from an older Inbox.
